cases.summary: The Department of Justice charged the defendant with theft after diamonds went missing from a locked shop chest in the Redmont market district. The shop owner reported the loss the same evening.
cases.arguments: Prosecution: block-interaction logs placed the defendant at the chest minutes before the items disappeared, and a witness saw them leaving the shop. Defence: the defendant claimed the shop owner had agreed to a sale in private messages, so the items were not taken unlawfully, but could not produce the messages.
cases.verdict: Guilty. The court found the logs and witness testimony credible and the claimed sale unsupported. The defendant was ordered to return the items' value to the shop owner and pay a fine.
cases.title: Commonwealth of Redmont v. ExampleCitizen

cases.summary: A construction company sued a client who refused to pay the final instalment for a completed mansion build, arguing the work did not match the agreed design.
cases.arguments: Plaintiff: submitted the signed contract, the approved design screenshots and photos of the finished build. Defendant: argued the roof material differed from the design and that this justified withholding payment.
cases.verdict: For the plaintiff. The difference was minor and did not amount to a material breach. The defendant was ordered to pay the outstanding instalment, reduced slightly to account for the roof material.
cases.title: Example Builders LLC v. ExampleClient

cases.summary: A congressional candidate challenged a new act banning all campaign signs within 50 blocks of the capitol, arguing it restricted free political expression protected by the Constitution.
cases.arguments: Plaintiff: the ban covered most of the city's public space and left no reasonable way to campaign there. Commonwealth: the act kept the capitol area clear and applied equally to every candidate.
cases.verdict: Partly unconstitutional. The court upheld a ban on signs directly around the capitol building but struck down the 50-block radius as broader than necessary.
cases.title: ExampleCandidate v. Commonwealth of Redmont

cases.summary: A landowner claimed their neighbour's new garden extended three blocks onto their plot and sought removal of the build plus compensation.
cases.arguments: Plaintiff: relied on their own measurements and screenshots of the plot before the garden was built. Defendant: pointed out the plaintiff had never registered an updated survey of the plot.
cases.verdict: Dismissed. Without an official plot record the court could not establish where the boundary lay. The plaintiff may refile after obtaining a survey.
cases.title: ExampleLandowner v. ExampleNeighbour

cases.summary: The Commonwealth appealed the Federal Court's ruling in [2026] FCR 1, which struck down part of the campaign sign ban.
cases.arguments: Commonwealth: the lower court failed to give enough weight to Congress's judgement about public order. Respondent: the lower court applied the correct test and its ruling should stand.
cases.title: In re [2026] FCR 1
